obverse.design: The obverse design of the coin features a central circle containing a Trident (Trishula), a major symbol of Hinduism, which is enclosed within a square frame inscribed with the King's name in Devanagari script, Shree Gyanendra Bir Bikram Shah Dev. Surrounding this central square are various Hinduism icons, including a crescent moon and sun at the top, a conch shell to the right, and other sacred motifs, while the bottom of the coin displays the Devanagari numerals (२० ६०) representing the year 2060 in the Vikram Samvat calendar.

reverse.design: Features the Janaki Mandir, a famous Hindu temple in Janakpur dedicated to the Goddess Sita 2 Rupees (२ रूपैयाँ).

obverse.design: The obverse of the coin features a striking depiction of Mount Everest, accompanied by the inscription (Sagarmatha,) which is the mountain's official name in Nepal. This side utilizes the Devanagari script for its lettering, displaying (सगरमाथा) along with the date (2066,) which follows the Vikram Samvat calendar.

reverse.design: On the reverse, the design showcases a traditional rural scene of a farmer ploughing a field with water buffaloes. This side incorporates both Devanagari and Latin scripts to identify the issuing country as (नेपाल NEPAL.) It also clearly states the coin's denomination as (2 Rupee) (२ रुपैयाँ).

obverse.design: The obverse of the 1 Rupee coin features a majestic depiction of Mount Everest in the center, highlighting Nepal's natural heritage. Above the mountain, the word (Nepal) is written in Devanagari script (नेपाल), while below the peak, the name (Sagarmatha)—the Nepali name for Mount Everest—is inscribed in Latin letters. Further below, (Nepal) is written in English, and the bottom of the coin displays the year 1077 in the Nepali Vikram Samvat calendar.

reverse.design: The reverse of the coin showcases a detailed outline of the map of Nepal in the middle, which is divided into its constituent states. In the background of the map, mountains are visible, and to the right, there is a distinct dot representing the number 1 in braille, enhancing accessibility. The top of the reverse bears the English value (Rs. One,) while the bottom features the value (१ रुपैया) (1 Rupee) in Devanagari script.
